title: Songbook and Garden Revisited
premise: Cyrus Sterling, keeper of her late grandfather's lighthouse and a stalled novelist, joins a small-town anonymous pen-pal program meant to pair strangers — but a clerical error pairs her with Wren Calloway, the woman who once broke up her engagement to Cyrus's brother and then vanished. Forced by the program's rules to correspond for one season without revealing their names, the two enemies slowly unmask old wounds: Cyrus's guilt over choosing duty to the lighthouse over love, and Wren's secret that she left town pregnant and alone. As letters turn into reluctant visits, shared garden work on the overgrown keeper's plot, and a storm that threatens the lighthouse itself, they must forgive themselves before they can forgive each other. In the end, Cyrus publishes the novel she wrote in those letters, Wren's daughter calls the lighthouse home, and both women choose love not as a second chance but as a first honest one.
about_author: Silas Brightwater is the pen name of a former coastal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and love letters donated to maritime museums. They write slow-burn romances about people who repair things — boats, gardens, and each other.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Cyrus Sterling's POV. She tends the automated lighthouse her grandfather kept by hand, writing a novel she can't finish and refusing the town's pity. Establishes her isolation, duty-bound grief, and wry voice. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: Dead Letters Wanted
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her best friend Odette bullies her into the Harborlight Anonymous Pen-Pal Program, a seasonal letter exchange run from the library. Cyrus signs up mostly to prove she won't be matched with anyone who matters. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Hardware Store
chapters.summary: Wren Calloway's POV. Wren returns to Port Merrow after nine years with her daughter Juniper, buying paint for a house she inherited. She recognizes the town, dreads recognition herself. Beat: dread disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: A Clerical Error
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The librarian misfiles two cards; Cyrus and Wren are paired as anonymous pen pals, neither knowing the other's identity — only that the handwriting feels familiar. First letters are stiff, hostile-adjacent politeness. Beat: uneasy curiosity.

chapters.title: Enemies, Presumably
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes from a mention of the lighthouse that her pen pal is likely Cyrus Sterling, whose engagement to Wren's ex she shattered years ago. She almost quits the program, then writes anyway. Beat: guilty compulsion.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus begins clearing her grandfather's ruined kitchen garden and complains about it in a letter; her pen pal replies with startlingly good advice about soil. Unknowingly, they collaborate. Beat: grudging respect.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback woven through present: how Wren fell for Daniel Sterling, ended his engagement to Cyrus, then fled when she learned she was pregnant and he chose his family's expectations. Beat: shame reframing into self-protection.

chapters.title: Letters About Fictional People
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Both women discuss their stalled lives through invented characters — Cyrus shares her unfinished novel's heroine; Wren critiques it sharply and correctly. The correspondence warms despite barbs. Beat: intellectual intimacy.

chapters.title: Juniper Asks About the Sea
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Six-year-old Juniper becomes fascinated by the lighthouse and asks endless questions Wren can't answer honestly. Wren starts walking her past it at a distance. Beat: tenderness tangled with avoidance.

chapters.title: The Storm Season Opens
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. First autumn gale knocks out the lighthouse's backup systems; Cyrus spends a night keeping watch manually as her grandfather did. She writes about it, moved, and her pen pal answers with unexpected tenderness. Beat: vulnerability through distance.

chapters.title: Odette Suspects Everything
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Odette notices Cyrus is happier and deduces the pen pal is local, maybe someone Cyrus knows. Cyrus denies it too quickly. Comic beat with an undertow of fear: what if it's her?

chapters.title: Paint and Proximity
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the hardware store, Wren and Cyrus collide face-to-face for the first time in nine years. Polite, frozen, devastating small talk. Neither reveals being pen pals. Beat: shock held under glass.

chapters.title: The Letter I Almost Burned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Shaken, Wren writes a letter confessing everything except her name — that she wronged someone here, that she doesn't deserve kindness. Cyrus reads it as a stranger's pain and responds with grace. Dramatic irony peaks. Beat: mercy misdirected.

chapters.title: Grafting
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following her pen pal's advice, Cyrus grafts apple cuttings from her grandfather's tree onto new rootstock — a metaphor she resists noticing. Meanwhile Wren appears at the garden gate offering help. First real conversation. Beat: cautious thaw.

chapters.title: Daniel Comes Back
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus's brother Daniel returns for their mother's birthday, forcing all three into one room. Old accusations surface; Daniel is now married elsewhere and bitter. Wren leaves early; Cyrus defends her, surprising herself. Beat: loyalty shifting sides.

chapters.title: What You Said in Your Sleep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Juniper repeats something overheard — that Mama writes to a friend at the lighthouse. Wren realizes Juniper has seen her mailing letters near the harbor. Panic: does Cyrus know? Beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Harvest Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus's pen pal sends her most open letter yet: about a daughter, about running, about wanting to stop being a person who leaves. Cyrus, certain her pen pal is a stranger, offers forgiveness 'for whatever you did.' Beat: grace given blind.

chapters.title: Reading Between the Lines
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren compares the harvest letter reply's phrasing to things Cyrus said at the hardware store. Certainty arrives like cold water. She keeps writing anyway — now knowingly. Beat: love beginning against will.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Truth
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Working the garden together, Wren nearly tells Cyrus the truth and instead says 'I'm not who you think I am.' Cyrus hears honesty, not warning. They share cider on the lighthouse steps. Beat: intimacy without confession.

chapters.title: The Program's Deadline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The library announces the reveal event: pen pals meet at season's end, six weeks away. Both women realize they'll be exposed publicly. Each privately decides to confess first — and each fails to. Beat: ticking clock installed.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Novel Gets Its Ending
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Inspired by the letters, Cyrus finishes her novel in a three-day fever — a story about a keeper who forgives a runaway. She mails the manuscript and tells her pen pal first. Beat: creative rebirth.

chapters.title: Juniper's School Play
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cyrus attends the school play to support Odette's nephew and watches Wren glow with maternal pride. Cyrus feels the past soften — and feels something new and unwelcome: attraction. Beat: enemy to something else.

chapters.title: The Photograph in the Logbook
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Sorting grandfather's logbooks, Cyrus finds a photo of young Wren at the lighthouse with Daniel — and a note in her grandfather's hand: 'That girl was kind to me in the hospital.' Cyrus's hatred loses its foundation. Beat: revision of memory.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A rainstorm traps them in the garden shed; close, laughing, breath-visible. Wren says 'There's something you should know' — and Juniper bangs on the door calling for her mum. Moment lost. Beat: frustration and relief entwined.

chapters.title: Odette Plays Detective
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Odette matches the pen-pal handwriting samples (she volunteers at the library) and confronts Cyrus: 'It's Wren Calloway, isn't it?' Cyrus refuses to believe it, then checks the reveal-event card stock against Wren's grocery lists. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: The Confrontation That Isn't
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cyrus shows up at Wren's house, letter in hand, ready to accuse — and finds Wren reading Cyrus's own novel excerpt aloud to Juniper. Cyrus leaves without speaking. Beat: accusation dissolving into ache.

chapters.title: What Duty Cost Me
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Long flashback chapter: young Cyrus choosing the lighthouse and family obligation over her own writing and a life abroad, letting everyone assume she was jilted rather than admitting she froze. Beat: self-forgiveness begins — she was never only the victim.

chapters.title: Two Letters, One Envelope
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Both women mail confessions the same day; a postal delay holds them. Each waits by their mailbox, each interprets silence as rejection. Beat: suspended dread, dramatic tension at its highest pre-climax.

chapters.title: The Gale
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A historic storm strikes; the lighthouse lamp fails and a fishing boat runs toward the rocks. Cyrus climbs the tower in dangerous conditions. Wren, seeing the dark beacon from town, drives into the gale with spare parts from the hardware store. Beat: crisis fuses them.

chapters.title: Lamp Room Confession
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Soaked and shaking in the lamp room, relit beam sweeping, Wren shouts the truth over the wind: she was the pen pal, she was the woman from nine years ago, she was sorry before she ever came back. Cyrus can't answer — the boat still needs the light. Beat: truth amid emergency.

chapters.title: After the Water Recedes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The boat is saved; the town celebrates its keepers. Cyrus, hollowed out, doesn't go to Wren. She rereads every letter and sees the whole arc of Wren's guilt and love she refused to name. Beat: grief before forgiveness.

chapters.title: Daniel's Version
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Daniel confronts Cyrus, demanding she side with him again; he reveals he knew Wren was pregnant and told her to leave. Cyrus sees her brother clearly for the first time and refuses. Beat: breaking the family spell.

chapters.title: The Empty Mailbox
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reveal night passes; Wren doesn't attend, sure Cyrus despises her. She packs boxes to leave Port Merrow. Juniper quietly puts a drawing of the lighthouse in the suitcase. Beat: lowest point.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus finally reads her grandfather's last unsent letter — to Wren, thanking her, telling her to come home someday. Cyrus understands forgiveness was never hers to gatekeep. She drives through the night. Beat: epiphany.

chapters.title: The House With the For Sale Sign
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus arrives as Wren loads the car. No grand speech — Cyrus hands her the grandfather's letter and the harvest letter, side by side. 'You were forgiven before I knew it was you.' Wren unpacks one box. Beat: reconciliation, understated.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Time skip to spring: the garden's grafted trees blossom; Wren and Juniper plant their own row. The town absorbs them as a pair without ceremony. Quiet domestic joy. Beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Reveal Event, Belatedly
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odette hosts a make-up reveal party where the whole town pretends surprise. Cyrus reads aloud the first hostile letter and the last tender one; laughter and tears. Wren's hand finds Cyrus's. Beat: public acknowledgment, communal warmth.

chapters.title: Songbook
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus's novel accepts publication; she dedicates it 'to my pen pal, who edited my life.' Wren reveals she kept every letter tied in ribbon — the songbook of the title. Beat: love named plainly.

chapters.title: Revisited
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. One year later: the three of them repaint the lighthouse railing, Juniper asking questions that now get honest answers. Wren reflects that she didn't get a second chance — she got a truer first one. Beat: peace earned.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Turning
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing. Evening scene: Cyrus logs the weather in her grandfather's ledger, adds Wren's handwriting beside hers; the lamp sweeps the water; the garden sleeps. Final image of continuity — duty and love no longer opposites. Beat: resolution, quiet and luminous.
